note: Pinned build inputs: pixi, Mojo, ninja, make, and pkg-config are exact; system clang, bpftool, gcc, zlib, cmake, and dev-only Python carry minimum floors (default install per environment). Verify with: pixi install && tools/build --check-toolchain. The pixi.lock file carries authoritative conda package hashes; this file records the selected versions and their provenance.

libbpf_source.note: System provides libbpf.so.1 runtime but no headers; build from this pinned source.

clang.note: Floor; verified with Ubuntu 26.04 clang 21.1.8 and Fedora 44 clang 22.1.8.

bpftool.note: Floor; verified with Ubuntu 26.04 bpftool 7.7.0 and Fedora 44 bpftool 7.6.0.

cmake.role: native build driver; default install in each environment

host_cc.role: host C compilation fallback; native builds use clang
host_cc.note: Floor; verified with Ubuntu 26.04 gcc 15.2.0 and Fedora 44 gcc 16.2.1.

libelf.note: Build input for the libbpf source build. Headers verified installable via apt on Ubuntu 26.04; Fedora 44 provides elfutils-libelf-devel 0.196. The native build step verifies with pkg-config and fails closed when they are absent.

zlib.note: Floor; Fedora 44 reports 1.3.1.zlib-ng via zlib-ng-compat-devel, which satisfies it.

linux_headers.role: UAPI headers (<linux/bpf.h>) for the bridge and fixtures
linux_headers.note: Backward-stable kernel UAPI; pinned for exact reproduction.

python.role: development validation only; never runtime collection

platform_floor.kernel: >= 7.0 for collection; passive inspection and offline work have no kernel floor
platform_floor.note: A version string is eligibility only. Each capability needs its own profile and live evidence.

decisions: D1: pixi (pixi.toml + pixi.lock) is the Mojo project manifest; one manifest per repository.
D2: Mojo 1.2.0 stable from the public max channel; nightly builds are not used.
D3: libbpf is built from the pinned v1.7.0 source tarball with hash check; no system-header dependency.

D4: System clang carries a minimum floor (21.1.8); its BPF backend is mature and this avoids a large conda toolchain. An exact string would single-distro the build, so bit-reproducibility is claimed only for CI-built artifacts. Revisit on BPF codegen issues.
D5: CMake + Ninja is the native build driver, invoked only through tools/build (single supported path).
D6: Validation tooling uses Python standard library only; no third-party Python dependencies.

D7: cmake is a build driver, not a codegen input: the check enforces a minimum version (default install per environment), not an exact pin. System clang, bpftool, gcc, zlib, and dev-only Python carry floors for the same multi-distro reason; pixi, Mojo, ninja, make, and pkg-config stay exact.
